source: CTDL xTRA Engineering Running Notes, Extraction Report - 2026.11.18 (Seth Alt), verbatim

findings.title: The silver stores a requisite ("PR: Consent.") as the description of a course that has none
findings.cause:
D1, requisites only (317 silver). The Studio rule falls back to the requisite text when there is no description.
- Marshall [CD 580](https://catalog.marshall.edu/graduate/courses-az/cd/): the silver value is "PR: Permission of chair.", extracted none.
- WVU [FIS 610L](http://catalog.wvu.edu/graduate/courses/): the silver value is "PR: Corequisite of FIS 610.Firearms Examination - FIS 610 Laboratory.", extracted none.
findings.assessment: leaving these empty is correct. The golden convention keeps requisites out of ceterms:description.

findings.title: The catalog runs the description into the "PR:" sentence with no full stop, so the reader takes it all as requisites
findings.cause:
D1b, [CS 558](http://catalog.wvu.edu/graduate/collegeofengineeringandmineralresources/) (WVU, 2 silver).
- The source is "PR: CS 350 or EE 465 or consent, requirements and QOS; multimedia data acquisition, … retrieval of multimedia data." There is no full stop between the requisite and the description.
findings.assessment: this is a real miss, but the catalog's own text is broken.

findings.title: The silver rule trims too much: it drops real description sentences after a "PR:" lead-in
findings.assessment: the extractor is right. WVU golden is 24/24.

findings.title: The silver keeps the requisite lead-in that the golden convention drops
findings.cause:
D3, the silver keeps the lead-in (198 silver). The same regex fails to match when the "PR:" sentence ends ".)" or the next sentence starts with "(", so the whole text, lead-in included, goes into silver.
- WVU [HIST 702](http://catalog.wvu.edu/graduate/courses/): the silver value starts "PR: HIST 701; (Reading knowledge of Latin … recommended.) Directed examination…". Extracted: "Directed examination…".
- AVC [IATH 265](https://avc.elumenapp.com/catalog/2026-27/course/iath265): the silver value starts "Limitation on enrollment: Physical examination and tryout required. Designed for…". Extracted: "Designed for…". AVC golden drops this lead-in and is 44/44.

findings.title: The baseline keeps the source's double spaces or line breaks
findings.cause:
D4, whitespace (8 golden, 225 silver).
- CCSF [SMBU 9793](https://ccsf.curricunet.com/catalog/iq/courses/3/152): "…a successful marketing␠␠strategy…" in the baseline, one space when extracted.
findings.assessment: this is the CCSF golden's own convention. It keeps whitespace no browser shows, and it is all of CCSF's golden partials.

findings.title: The baseline keeps a space before a full stop after a course link ("ARTS 71103 .")
findings.cause:
D5, UALR spacing at a course link (92 silver). For [ARTS 71203](https://catalog.ualr.edu/preview_course_nopop.php?catoid=42&coid=131139):
- the baseline is "Continuation of ARTS 71103 . At completion…";
- the extracted value is "Continuation of ARTS 71103. At completion…".
The source has whitespace between the linked course code and the full stop. The baseline keeps it; the extractor removes it.

findings.title: The silver value stops at a line break in the source
The silver keeps only the closing line ("Three hours lecture. Three credit hours.")
findings.cause: D7, the UALR silver keeps only the closing line (2 silver). [CHEM 43003](https://catalog.ualr.edu/preview_course_nopop.php?catoid=43&coid=139497) and [CHEM 53003](https://catalog.ualr.edu/preview_course_nopop.php?catoid=42&coid=139498) have silver "Three hours lecture. Three credit hours." The extracted value is the course's full description paragraph.

findings.title: A requisite lead-in with no colon ("Prerequisite Completion of…") isn't dropped
findings.cause:
D8, AVC [FTEC 295A](https://avc.elumenapp.com/catalog/2026-27/course/ftec295a) (1 silver). The extracted value starts:
Prerequisite Completion of FTEC 111.
Corequisite: Concurrent enrollment in FTEC 295AL.
The baseline starts at "Combined with FTEC 295B…". The lead-in has no colon, so the lead-in rule doesn't drop it.

findings.title: The course page is labelled Course, but no course code is found where the reader looks, so no resource id and no records are written
findings.cause:
M1: no course code where the reader looks.
course_code() looks for a code at the start of the title, and two UALR title forms don't fit:
- Law School: the code comes at the end of the title. 195 silver, 4 golden.
  - Example: [Administrative Law - LAWW 65043](https://catalog.ualr.edu/preview_course_nopop.php?catoid=44&coid=139236). The baseline identifier is LAWW65043.
- Honors: codes like HNRS 103H1 have a section suffix the code pattern doesn't accept. 14 silver, 1 golden.
  - Example: [Scholars Colloquium II](https://catalog.ualr.edu/preview_course_nopop.php?catoid=43&coid=137425). The baseline is HNRS103H1.
findings.fix: this is the course code follow-up. ceterms:identifier and the resource id both come from course_identifier(), so fixing course_code() recovers all three properties.

findings.title: Discovery labels the page Unknown, so it isn't read as a course
findings.cause:
M2: not labelled Course.
- CCSF (176 silver, 13 golden), 23 department pages:
  - Example: [ccsf.curricunet.com/catalog/iq/courses/3/142](https://ccsf.curricunet.com/catalog/iq/courses/3/142) lists "PLS 1 Introduction to Paralegal Studies", "PLS 2…" and more.
  - Discovery counts too few course codes on these pages to call them Course.
  - The reason: CurriQunet codes like PLS 1 and PARA 51 have a one- or two-digit number, and the code pattern refuses those so that it doesn't read "GOAL 1" as a course.
  - Read directly, these pages give 69/69 golden identifiers.
- UALR (5 silver): one-course pages whose titles discovery can't read as a course:
  - 3 Honors pages, such as [HNRS 121H3](https://catalog.ualr.edu/preview_course_nopop.php?catoid=43&coid=137429);
  - [a page that prints two dual-listed numbers](https://catalog.ualr.edu/preview_course_nopop.php?catoid=43&coid=136179) (baseline GERO4900349003);
  - [one CPSI page](https://catalog.ualr.edu/preview_course_nopop.php?catoid=43&coid=137732).

findings.title: Discovery labels the page Credential, so it isn't read as a course
findings.cause:
M3: labelled Credential.
- UARK (4 silver; golden 3 name, 2 description, 1* identifier): certification pages such as [retort-processing-certification](https://training.uark.edu/portal/training?cmd=catalog&course=retort-processing-certification) and [complete-bpcs-certification](https://training.uark.edu/portal/training?cmd=catalog&course=complete-bpcs-certification).
  - The address names one course, but the page lists its own requirements. The guard (lists_its_own_requirements) therefore keeps the Course rules from labelling it, and the page stays a Credential.
- UALR (1 silver): [EDLE 90003 "Doctoral Seminar and Scholarly Writing"](https://catalog.ualr.edu/preview_course_nopop.php?catoid=42&coid=132248). Its description reads like program requirements.

findings.title: The course is read, but it has no description apart from requisites (see D1)
